newsitem.title: USA: Russian immigrant accused of being negligent parent.
newsitem.headline: Russian immigrant accused of being negligent parent.

text.p: Russian immigrant Tatiana Glotova appeared in court on Wednesday on charges she left her 7-year-old son, Dennis, alone in a New York City park for two hours while she worked.

Glotova, 25, of suburban Paterson, New Jersey, denied she left the boy unsupervised. According to a statement read in court, Glotova, a messenger at a design and photography studio, said her boss sent her to do a job in a building near the park.
"I could see the boy from my building. I didn't know I couldn't leave him outside," she said.
Glotova was released without bond on charges of endangering the welfare of a child and was due back in court July 7. If convicted, she could face up to a year in prison.

Her son was placed in foster care while the case was investigated, said Maggie Lear, a spokeswoman for the Administration for Children's Services. Lear said the child was unharmed and there were no signs of abuse.

Glotova was arrested on Tuesday when she returned to fetch her son after leaving him alone in Madison Park for two hours. Parents supervising their children in the park's playground had alerted a police officer to the unattended child.

Last month, Danish officials charged city authorities with overreacting after they arrested Annette Sorensen, a Danish actress, for leaving her 14-month-old daughter in a baby stroller on the sidewalk while she and the infant's father had drinks in a restaurant.

Sorensen and representatives of the Danish government said that leaving babies in carriages outside shops and restaurants was common in Denmark. The case against Sorenson and the child's father was dropped.
In April, a Russian couple, Natalia and Peter Jestyrev, were arrested after they left their 4-year-old daughter home alone while they partied until dawn at a Manhattan club.
They told police it was customary to leave a small child alone in their home country. Charges against the couple were pending.
